bureau: CIASA credit registry (Central Bank of Sudan)
note: The IFC and Arab Monetary Fund's Arab Credit Reporting Guide (2015) on Sudan's credit registry: negative information is kept five years once paid, and until paid while it isn't; registered as secondary, the Central Bank of Sudan's own rule not read. No source read states how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported, so the days are the game's reading: the bureau's next monthly update. Re-read 2026-11-03: the Credit Inquiry and Classification Law 2011, on the Central Bank of Sudan's site, sets up the agency (CIASA) under article 3 and defines its information as payment history going back at least five years; it states no rule that negative data is kept five years once paid and until paid while it isn't, which is the guide's and is left to regulations not found, so the years stay secondary.

sources.title: IFC and Arab Monetary Fund, Arab Credit Reporting Guide (2015)
sources.said: whereas negative information is kept ... for five years if all the payments have been made

sources.title: Central Bank of Sudan (cbos.gov.sd): قانون الاستعلام والتصنيف الائتماني لسنة 2011 (Credit Inquiry and Classification Law 2011), full text
sources.said: "المعلومات": يقصد بها سلوك أو أنماط السداد لمعلومات تاريخية ترجع إلى خمس سنوات على الأقل وتعبر عن مدى التزام العملاء بالسداد في المواعيد المحددة، وتشمل معلومات ايجابية ومعلومات سلبية، ... "الوكالة": يقصد بها وكالة الاستعلام والتصنيف الائتماني المنشأة بموجب أحكام المادة 3، ... الاحتفاظ بطلبات الاستعلام لمدة لا تقل عن سنتين وفقا للضوابط والإجراءات التي تحددها اللوائح
